facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: After many mistakes Pinocchio began to understand something. Every time he told the truth he felt a small weight lift. Every time he lied the weight came back heavier than before. The fairy had always known when he was lying anyway. But even without her Pinocchio saw that honesty felt better. It was hard in the moment but easy to carry afterward. Integrity means honesty.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: After many adventures and many mistakes Pinocchio began to understand something important. Every time he had told the truth he had felt a small weight lift from his chest. Every time he had lied he had felt that weight return doubled and heavier than before. The Blue Fairy had always known when he was lying — the nose made that quite impossible to hide. But even without the nose Pinocchio was learning that honesty felt better in the long run. It was uncomfortable in the moment but it left nothing heavy or secret to carry around afterward. A person of integrity does not choose honesty because it is easy — they choose it because it is right. Integrity means honesty.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: After many adventures and many very expensive mistakes, Pinocchio slowly began to understand something important about himself and about the nature of truth. Every time he had told the truth about something difficult, he had felt a small and unexpected weight lift slightly from the center of his wooden chest. Every time he had told a lie to escape a difficult conversation, he had felt that same weight return afterward, doubled and heavier than it had been before. The Blue Fairy had always known exactly when he was lying, of course, because his growing nose made concealment practically impossible in her presence. But even without the tell-tale nose, Pinocchio was slowly learning on his own that honesty simply felt better over any significant period of time. It was uncomfortable in the moment, and sometimes sharply so — but it left nothing heavy or secret that he had to carry around with him afterward. A person of genuine integrity, he came to see, does not choose honesty because honesty happens to be easy or pleasant in the particular moment. They choose it because it is right, and because the alternative — a life spent maintaining a network of small deceptions — is exhausting in ways that can never quite be repaid. Integrity means honesty.
